shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/pillar carved in relief
relief carving covering the full front face
horizontal registers or banded divisions of the surface
schematic animal/creature forms integrated into the design
a human or humanoid figure with visible arms
repeated small motifs arranged in a row across the top
monument shown in situ within a rubble/landscape setting
justification: Both are tall rectangular monoliths whose front faces are entirely covered with relief organised into stacked horizontal registers, including a row of repeated motifs near the top and a humanoid figure with arms lower down. The decisive difference is density and depth: A is a sparse, flat, shallow-cut composition of isolated schematic creatures with wide blank ground, while B is a densely packed, deeply undercut and near-symmetrical composition dominated by a single frontal figure with elaborate surrounding ornament, and the two are also presented in wholly different media (colour photograph vs. line engraving).
